en: Praise to Potalaka: Victory to the Teacher of the worlds of Siddhas, Suras, and Asuras,
whose pair of feet rests upon the lotus seat!
I perpetually bow down to the one who holds the lotus of the ten perfections and other qualities, the supreme compassionate one. || 1 ||
Victory to the Sage Lord Susthitasusthita, who has received boons from many millions of lords of men,
and who has brought beings across to the further shore of the ocean of existence!
Who brings about the welfare of those beings who have come for refuge. || 2 ||
Wearing a beautiful form with a lotus seat,
bearing the Tathāgata Amitābha upon his crown,
and possessing a sublime body adorned and radiant with lotuses.
It possesses a splendor as beautiful and radiant as nine suns. || 3 ||
His face was adorned with fingers and nails as soft as copper; his gentle countenance possessed a radiance equal to the orb of the moon;
his body was worthy of worship by those who possess the qualities of the six super-knowledges.
Adorned with excellent, well-placed anklets and necklaces. || 4 ||
His pair of cheeks was adorned with jeweled earrings,
his deep voice resembled the thundering of clouds,
and he made his dwelling illuminating mountain caves.
One hundred [years] of bull-vehicle, swan, deer, and elephant [ages]. || 5 ||
Praised by hosts of sages and gods, possessing the supreme awakening that takes the form of a Victor,
the Lord of bipeds and Sovereign of the gods.
It effects the liberation and deliverance of many beings. || 6 ||
His left hand is beautifully adorned with a banner and an umbrella;
he bears the likeness of sandalwood incense from the Malaya mountains,
and he holds a garland of lotuses, blue water-lilies, and *pāṭali* flowers.
Then I bow down to the one who causes the prosperity of Pāṭaliputra. || 7 ||
It dispels fever and disease, removes leprosy, bestows abundant wisdom, destroys the dense clouds of sin,
brings about auspiciousness, and provides the path that destroys the nine miserable states of existence.
The Lord of the Universe, who is non-dual with compassion and suchness. || 8 ||
The *Potalakāṣṭaka* of the glorious Āryāvalokiteśvara is complete.
